newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-Kredyt Bank to expand by PBI merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Kredyt Bank to expand by PBI merger.

text.p: Poland's Kredyt Bank SA will merge with the Polish Investment Bank SA (PBI) to become the country's eighth largest bank in terms off assets, its president said on Friday.

Earlier today Kredyt president Stanislaw Pacuk and the National Bank of Poland signed an agreement for Kredyt's purchase of all of PBI, previously controlled by the central bank, and 92.36 percent of the ailing Prosper Bank SA for 205 million zlotys and investment guarantees.

"We did not purchase these banks to keep them independent, we want to merge PBI with Kredyt Bank to form a strong new banking institution, which will be (the country's) eighth largest in terms of assets," Pacuk told a news conference.
"As far as Prosper Bank is concerned, our investments in that bank will be spread out over time and when Prosper is restructured it will be merged," he added.
Kredyt Bank vowed to invest in Prosper 160 million zlotys which is roughly equivalent to its debts and increase the bank's capital to five million Ecu within several years.
It also will raise the share capital of PBI by 100 million zlotys within a year and pledged to invest another 25 million zlotys in PBI's computer infrastructure.
The deal also envisions the possibility of PBI employees buying some of the bank's shares.
Pacuk said that Kredyt Bank was mulling changing its name to make use of PBI's domestically known retail banking name.
He said that Kredyt will use its own funds for the purchase of the two banks and that it planned to use its upcoming share issue to raise some of the cash for the deal.
"The funds (for the purchase of PBI and Prosper Bank) will come from own capital," Pacuk said, but declined to give any specific details.
Kredyt Bank will offer 10 million new shares at 8 zlotys each to large investors and another two million to small investors between April 21 and April 25.
It will also offer 847,000 shares to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
Pacuk said that after the issue Belgian Kredietbank NV will increase its holding in Kredyt to about 10 percent from 7.5 percent.
Deputy central bank president Witold Kozinski, also present, said Kredyt outbid Austria's Creditanstalt, the other shortlisted bidder, and U.S. GE Capital, which did not make the final cut-off.
"We picked Kredyt Bank because it had a better offer...and we are happy because fate has decided that the Polish banking system will be strengthened through this deal," Kozinski said.
Kozinski said Creditanstalt's bid was 200 million zlotys and a similar investment plan, but that the Austrian bank wanted the central bank to guarantee part of PBI's credit portfolio.
At the end of 1996 PBI had capital of 197.1 million zlotys, a balance sheet total of 4.56 billion zlotys and recorded a 55.2 million zloty net profit that year.
Prosper Bank, 93-percent owned by the central bank, has capital of 16.1 million zlotys and an accumulated loss of 161 million zlotys. It has a balance sheet total of 557 million zlotys.
Under the conditions of the tender investors who wanted to buy PBI were also required to buy Prosper Bank.
At the end of 1996 Kredyt Bank had capital of 219 million zlotys, making a net profit that year of 23.2 million zlotys. Its balance sheet total was 1.07 billion zlotys.
